# kind: # Every row is a recorded beat, in playback order. line1 and line2 become the subtitle; the designed scenes
# (friday, tickets, turn, adopt, outro) carry their own on-screen text, so they have no subtitle.

name: friday
spoken: Friday, four p.m. A partner goes live Monday, and their web app needs every Meridian API. It is one line of CORS configuration, copied into twenty-four APIs owned by six teams.

name: blocked
line1: NovaPay's web app calls all 24 Meridian APIs through Tyk Gateway: 23 refuse it
line2: The one that answers, Payments, allows every website
spoken: The partner's web app is refused by twenty-three APIs. The one that answers, Payments, allows every website.

name: drift
line1: Meridian runs 24 APIs, and each keeps its own copy of the CORS rules
line2: No single place says what the rule is
spoken: Meridian runs twenty-four APIs, and each keeps its own copy of the rules. No single place says what the rule is.

name: drift-api
line2: It was opened up during an incident and never closed
spoken: Payments' copy allows every website. It was opened up during an incident, and nobody noticed.

name: tickets
spoken: So one line becomes twenty-four tickets, reviews and deploys. Some get stuck. Monday comes and the launch is not ready.

name: turn
spoken: The rule is the same in every API. So why is it stored twenty-four times? Tyk five sixteen adds API Fragments.

name: create
line1: Tyk 5.16: create a Fragment and paste in the bank's CORS standard
line2: It is stored once, under Assets in Tyk Dashboard
spoken: The platform team creates a Fragment and pastes in the bank's CORS standard, once.

name: name
line1: Name it. APIs will point at it as fragment://cors-browser-apps
line2: Saved. No API uses it yet
spoken: They name it and save it. No API uses it yet.

name: adopt
spoken: Each API swaps its own copy for a one-line reference. Four copies had drifted, including Payments; now they follow the standard.

name: usage
line1: All 24 APIs now reference the one Fragment
line2: And the Dashboard lists every API that uses it
spoken: All twenty-four APIs now reference one Fragment, and the Dashboard lists every one of them.

name: edit
line1: Monday's launch: add NovaPay's origin to the Fragment
spoken: Now the partner launch: add NovaPay's origin to the Fragment. One edit, one save.

name: allowed
line1: The same page, reloaded: all 24 APIs accept NovaPay
line2: No API was edited or redeployed
spoken: Reload the partner app. All twenty-four APIs accept it. No API was edited or redeployed.

name: badge-api
line1: Payments now follows the standard: the wildcard is gone
line2: The setting is read-only in the API and names its Fragment
spoken: Payments now follows the standard, the wildcard is gone, and the API shows where the setting comes from.

name: guard
line1: A mistake: a value of the wrong type
line2: Tyk checks all 24 APIs first and refuses the save
spoken: A mistake: a value of the wrong type. Tyk checks every API that uses the Fragment, and refuses the save.

name: outro
spoken: Twenty-four copies became one Fragment. Four drifted APIs are back in line, and the partner launched with one edit.
